sections.h2: Which Douglas County offices touch your tax bill?
sections.html:
Douglas County divides the work between an appraisal team and an elected collector. Appraisal sets values and handles appeals on behalf of the Board of Assessors. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and takes homestead forms, and the commissioner's website walks through the bill, notices, exemptions and the delinquent list.

  • Appraisal Department: write to 8700 Hospital Dr., Douglasville, GA 30134 or call 770-920-7228. Walk-in filing is on the annex's second floor at 6200 Fairburn Rd.
  • Tax Commissioner: ground-level office in the Government Annex, serving the public weekdays except for a lunch closure at noon, with the last line cut off early to allow it.
  • Finance Department: publishes millage rate documents and hearing dates, and its 2026 packet carries a September 4 revision.

Field appraisers also canvass neighborhoods. The county's notice to property owners explains that these visits cover permit follow-up, new construction, additions, remodels, sales, appeals and returns, with measuring and photographing along the way. Each wears a photo badge and drives a marked vehicle.

sections.h2: When were Douglas County's 2026 assessment notices mailed and when did appeals close?
sections.html:
The mailing date for the 2026 annual notices was June 16, 2026. Appeals closed at 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026. The department posts in bold capitals that it cannot extend that date, and it recommends filing ahead of time while keeping your own copy in case the online system misbehaves.

Notices usually land between April 15 and July 1, with the 45 days measured from the date printed on the notice. Owners can post the form, hand it in at the annex, or use the online property search, and the parking lot dropbox covers evenings. Faxed or emailed forms are turned away, and anyone filing for an owner needs a signed authorization letter.

Request your property record card, plus the comparable sales the county holds, before you commit to an appeal. Boats, aircraft and business equipment get a notice only if the value shifts or the county rejects a return filed in the first quarter.

sections.h2: How does a Douglas County appeal move from the assessors to court?
sections.html:
An appeal advances in stages, and you can walk away at whichever stage gives you a fair number. The default track ends before a Board of Equalization seated by the grand jury.

  1. The assessors take a fresh look and mail a written answer, called the 30-day letter, that states whether the value changed.
  2. If the value holds, the file moves to the Board of Equalization automatically. If it drops and you are satisfied, the appeal simply lapses once the 30 days expire.
  3. If it changes and you still disagree, say so in writing before the 30 days end.
  4. The Board of Equalization mails notice of a hearing date, and the county recommends appearing with your own proof of market value.
  5. After the hearing, either party can take the result to Superior Court in the next 30 days after mailing, and the owner pays a $25 filing fee at the court clerk's office.

Other routes open when you file. Arbitration looks at value alone. A hearing officer handles non-homestead parcels valued above $500,000 and rules on value and uniformity. Superior Court directly needs the assessors' agreement and allows every kind of argument. The state's four grounds for appeal are taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions can Douglas County owners claim?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner takes homestead applications online and at the counter year-round, with April 1 as the cutoff for the cycle in progress. To qualify you must be both the owner and a resident as of January 1, and the proof the county asks for is a state ID or driver's license plus a vehicle registration carrying the homestead address. The Revenue Department adds a second window: the 45 days after a notice.

Exemption types listed by the county:

  • The standard homestead exemption.
  • Age 62 and age 65 senior exemptions, plus a 65 fixed-income version with an income requirement.
  • Disability, supported by two kinds of proof or certificates from two doctors, with a Social Security Administration letter.
  • Disabled veteran, shown by a VA statement of service-connected benefits paid at 100 percent on January 1.
  • Surviving spouses of armed forces members killed in action, and of police officers or firefighters killed on duty.

The Revenue Department's exemption page also names Douglas among counties with a valuation freeze, meaning a base-year figure holds the taxable value while the owner lives there. The Tax Commissioner can give the base year and the conditions.

sections.h2: What do Douglas County's housing numbers show?
sections.html:
About 720 residents share each of Douglas County's 200 land square miles. Growth runs at 6.9 percent over the 2020 base, to an estimated 154,293 people, and the Census Bureau logged 801 building permits in 2025. Workers spend 33.2 minutes getting to work on average.

Because about two of every three occupied homes have an owner living in them, an assessment jump reaches many households together. Set the value on your notice beside these typical figures and beside nearby sales before choosing to appeal. Residents 65 and older make up 13.8 percent of the population, and owners without a mortgage report typical monthly costs of $507.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill if you sell in Douglas County?
sections.html:
Under Georgia practice, ownership on January 1 fixes who owes for the year, and a later sale returns nothing to the seller. The state's FAQ describes a 60-day payment window and December 20 as the common due date. Douglas County's bill date and your parcel's balance come from the Tax Commissioner.

Look on the commissioner's site for the delinquent list, upcoming tax sales and excess funds, which will show any unpaid earlier year. Liens from county taxes are recorded on the general execution docket at the clerk, and the commissioner can confirm whether your parcel has one.

Dividing a lot before you sell starts with a survey submitted to the Zoning Administrator. After the approved, stamped survey is recorded, new deeds are signed and filed with the clerk, while a deed specialist inside Appraisal updates the tax records. Heirs and delinquent owners sometimes pick a no-repair cash sale, with the tax paid at closing.

faqs.q: Has the Douglas County 2026 appeal period ended?
faqs.a: Yes. Notices were mailed on June 16, 2026, and the period ran out at 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026, without extensions. New notices will start a new 45 days.

faqs.q: Will Douglas County take an appeal by fax or email?
faqs.a: No. Post it, bring it to the annex or use the online property search. If a representative files, include a letter of authorization.

faqs.q: How much is the Superior Court fee for a Douglas County appeal?
faqs.a: A $25 filing fee goes to the Clerk of Superior Court, and the owner tells the assessors in writing. Owner or assessors can appeal a Board of Equalization decision inside 30 days of its mailing.

faqs.q: Where does a Douglas County homestead application go?
faqs.a: To the Tax Commissioner, either online or in person. Bring a state ID or driver's license and a vehicle registration showing the house address. You need to own and occupy the home on January 1, and April 1 is the usual cutoff.

faqs.q: If I sell in spring, who owes Douglas County's tax for the year?
faqs.a: The person who owned it on January 1 owes for all twelve months, with no partial-year refund from Georgia. Your contract and settlement statement divide the cost with the buyer, so ask the Tax Commissioner for the balance first.
